name: Maple Syrup
land_types_note: Tapped from standing sugar maple forest (Quebec, Ontario, New Brunswick, US Northeast). The forest is kept, not cleared, but is managed for maple.

source.title: USDA FoodData Central
source.note: Maple Syrup — nutrition: USDA SR Legacy 'Syrups, maple' (fdcId 169661) per 100 g: 260 kcal, 0.04 g protein, 0.06 g fat, 0.007 g sat fat, 67.04 g carbs, 60.46 g sugars, 12 mg sodium, 32.39 g water; converted to per gram.

source.title: USDA FoodData Central
source.note: Maple Syrup — yield_fraction: syrup is sold and eaten as produced; nothing is discarded.

source.title: The Maple News — Season summaries (Quebec Maple Syrup Producers harvest reports)
source.note: Maple Syrup — yield_kg_ha: Quebec average yield 3.76 lb/tap (mean of 2020 and 2022–2025 QMSP harvests) = 1.71 kg/tap × 250 taps/ha (Perennia: 200–300 taps/ha in good sugar woods) = 425 kg syrup/ha/yr.

source.title: Perennia — Characteristics of a Good Sugar Maple Stand
source.note: Maple Syrup — soil_erosion: 0; sap is collected from standing forest with no soil disturbance.

source.title: Perennia — Characteristics of a Good Sugar Maple Stand
source.note: Maple Syrup — pesticide_kg_ha: 0; sugarbushes are not routinely sprayed (occasional insect-outbreak spraying ignored).

source.title: Perennia — Characteristics of a Good Sugar Maple Stand
source.note: Maple Syrup — fertilizer_kg_ha: 0; sugarbushes are not routinely fertilized (occasional liming ignored).

source.title: Perennia — Characteristics of a Good Sugar Maple Stand
source.note: Maple Syrup — tillage_events_per_year: 0; standing forest, never tilled.

source.title: CIRAIG — Is maple syrup good for the planet?
source.note: Maple Syrup — emissions_per_kg: AGECO study via CIRAIG — ~600 g CO2e per can of Quebec syrup (2021). A standard Quebec can is 540 mL × 1.33 kg/L = 0.72 kg syrup → 0.84 kg CO2e/kg. Over half is evaporation; ~50% of syrup boiled with oil.

source.title: Checkoway, Lewis & Keoleian (2024) — Carbon and Energy Footprinting across Archetypes for U.S. Maple Syrup Production (Environmental Science & Technology)
source.note: Maple Syrup — emissions_per_kg (US): large US producers 3.5–7 kg CO2e per US gallon (electric to oil-fired), midpoint 5.25 ÷ 5.03 kg syrup/gal (3.785 L × 1.33 kg/L) = 1.04 kg CO2e/kg. Large producers make most US syrup; small wood/oil operations are far higher (18–118 kg/gal).

source.title: Scott et al. (2004) — Changes in Carbon Storage and Net Carbon Exchange One Year After an Initial Shelterwood Harvest at Howland Forest, ME (Environmental Management)
source.note: Maple Syrup — co2_capture_kg_ha_yr: unharvested northeastern forest at Howland, Maine stores ~1.8 Mg C/ha/yr = 6,600 kg CO2/ha/yr. Mixed conifer–hardwood stand used as a proxy for a sugar maple forest.

source.title: The Maple News — Season summaries (Quebec Maple Syrup Producers harvest reports)
source.note: availability_gg: Quebec mean harvest 194.8 million lb (2020, 2022–2025) = 88,367 t; Quebec ≈ 66% of world (90.7% of Canada × Canada 73% of world, CBV Institute 2024) → world ≈ 133,000 t = 133 Gg.

name: Cane Sugar
land_types_note: Brazil (~40% of world cane, mostly former cerrado and Atlantic Forest in São Paulo), India and Pakistan (hot, largely irrigated plains), Thailand and southern China (tropical lowlands).

source.title: USDA FoodData Central
source.note: Cane Sugar — nutrition: USDA SR Legacy 'Sugars, granulated' (fdcId 169655) per 100 g: 387 kcal, 0 g protein, 0 g fat, 99.98 g carbs, 99.8 g sugars, 1 mg sodium; converted to per gram.

source.title: USDA FoodData Central
source.note: Cane Sugar — yield_fraction: yield_kg_ha is already kg of sugar, so nothing further is discarded.

source.title: Our World in Data — Crop Yields
source.note: Cane Sugar — yield_kg_ha: world sugarcane yield 73.1 t cane/ha (OWID/FAOSTAT mean 2020–2024) × ~11% sugar recovery (India 10.1% in 2023-24; Brazil ~138 kg recoverable sugar/t cane, USDA FAS) ≈ 8,000 kg sugar/ha/yr.

source.title: Mekonnen & Hoekstra (2010) — The Green, Blue and Grey Water Footprint of Crops and Crop Products (UNESCO-IHE Report 47)
source.note: Cane Sugar — water_per_kg: global average water footprint of refined cane sugar, 1,782 L/kg (green 1,184 + blue 487 + grey 111).

source.title: Mekonnen & Hoekstra (2010) — The Green, Blue and Grey Water Footprint of Crops and Crop Products (UNESCO-IHE Report 47)
source.note: Cane Sugar — green_water_per_kg: refined cane sugar, global average.

source.title: Mekonnen & Hoekstra (2010) — The Green, Blue and Grey Water Footprint of Crops and Crop Products (UNESCO-IHE Report 47)
source.note: Cane Sugar — blue_water_per_kg: refined cane sugar, global average. Much of India and Pakistan's cane is irrigated.

source.title: Mekonnen & Hoekstra (2010) — The Green, Blue and Grey Water Footprint of Crops and Crop Products (UNESCO-IHE Report 47)
source.note: Cane Sugar — grey_water_per_kg: refined cane sugar, global average.

source.title: Soil erosion on the Brazilian sugarcane cropping system: An overview (Geography and Sustainability, 2022)
source.note: Cane Sugar — soil_erosion: median of 43 soil-loss outcomes from 18 Brazilian studies under conventional tillage = 7.2 t/ha/yr (range by method 2–28).

source.title: Reis, Victória Filho, Andrade & Barroso (2019) — Use of Herbicides in Sugarcane in the São Paulo State (Planta Daninha)
source.note: Cane Sugar — pesticide_kg_ha: herbicide use on São Paulo sugarcane rose from 3.68 kg/ha (2010) to 5.00 kg/ha (2014). Insecticides (e.g. fipronil) add a little on top and are not counted.

source.title: Effect of Organic and Mineral Phosphate Fertilization of the Plant Cane and First Ratoon on the Second Ratoon in the Brazilian Cerrado (Agronomy, 2025)
source.note: Cane Sugar — fertilizer_kg_ha: Brazilian plant cane and ratoon get ~90 kg N + 80 kg K2O per cycle, plus ~50 kg P2O5 (study range 0–110) ≈ 220 kg/ha/yr.

source.title: Soil erosion on the Brazilian sugarcane cropping system: An overview (Geography and Sustainability, 2022)
source.note: Cane Sugar — tillage_events_per_year: the field is subsoiled, plowed and harrowed (~3 passes) only when cane is replanted, about every 6 years; ratoon years are not tilled. 3 ÷ 6 ≈ 0.5.

source.title: Our World in Data — GHG Emissions per kg of Food (Poore & Nemecek 2018)
source.note: Cane Sugar — emissions_per_kg: Poore & Nemecek (2018) global mean for cane sugar, 3.2 kg CO2e/kg (cradle to retail, includes land-use change).

source.title: Reis, Victória Filho, Andrade & Barroso (2019) — Use of Herbicides in Sugarcane in the São Paulo State (Planta Daninha)
source.note: Cane Sugar — glyphosate kg_ha: ~20% of sugarcane herbicide use in São Paulo × 5.0 kg/ha total ≈ 1.0 kg/ha. Used for burndown before replanting.

source.title: Reis, Victória Filho, Andrade & Barroso (2019) — Use of Herbicides in Sugarcane in the São Paulo State (Planta Daninha)
source.note: Cane Sugar — atrazine kg_ha: ~14.5% of sugarcane herbicide use in São Paulo × 5.0 kg/ha total ≈ 0.73 kg/ha.

source.title: Reis, Victória Filho, Andrade & Barroso (2019) — Use of Herbicides in Sugarcane in the São Paulo State (Planta Daninha)
source.note: Cane Sugar — 2,4-D kg_ha: ~10.6% of sugarcane herbicide use in São Paulo × 5.0 kg/ha total ≈ 0.53 kg/ha.

source.title: Wilmar International Annual Report 2024 — Our Sugar Journey
source.note: availability_gg: world cane sugar production ~152 million t in 2023/24 (~85% of the ~180 Mt world total, the rest is beet) = 152,000 Gg.
